method: Actual JFEM-Boxer, loaded source BDF for model views and the retained native archive for modal views; direct CDP PNG capture. No postprocessing.

images.title: Solid model
images.caption: Complete uniform-shell CRM wingbox. This adaptation has 23,738 nodes, 25,055 quadrilateral shells and 242 property regions.

images.title: Finite element mesh
images.caption: The complete shell mesh. This model contains no bar or rod elements: the source stiffener effect is smeared into the shell properties.

images.title: Translucent structure
images.caption: Translucent shell surfaces reveal ribs and spar webs inside the closed box.

images.title: Property regions
images.caption: Property ID colors identify regions. The isotropic adaptation uses the same 20 mm thickness and material in every region; this view does not imply a varying thickness field.

images.title: Properties in Boxer
images.caption: Actual JFEM-Boxer interface with the imported source deck and its structural property display.

images.title: Structural constraints
images.caption: Source-deck constraints, including the root and side-of-body restraints. Constraints are obtained from the BDF, not inferred from the mode shapes.

images.title: Internal ribs and spars
images.caption: Skin property regions are hidden using the normal entity visibility controls. Remaining shells are rendered with their physical thickness.

images.title: Inboard structure
images.caption: Selected inboard spar-web and rib properties, with the skins hidden and 20 mm shell thickness shown. Other regions are hidden, not removed from the FE model.

images.title: Exploded property regions
images.caption: Normal Boxer property explosion, spread radially about the model centroid. This separation changes the view only.

images.title: Inboard mesh detail
images.caption: Selected spar-web and rib patches shown at their reference surfaces with element edges.

images.title: Mode 1
images.caption: First recorded mode of the uniform isotropic adaptation. Frequency 1.682655 Hz. Color shows normalized element-mean displacement magnitude; eigenvector sign and amplitude are arbitrary. The undeformed mesh is a reference. Peak displayed translation is 2.6 m, chosen solely for visibility.
